one_line_contribution: Per-instance retrieval in procedural agent memory (ExpeL/ReasoningBank/Memp-style) can be replaced end-to-end by a fixed, verbatim, top-frequency subset of the same bank at no accuracy cost whenever the retriever's top-k sets are already near-identical across queries, and a rollout-free mean-pairwise-Jaccard statistic predicts out of sample both when that holds and whether injecting more items helps or hurts.
closest_prior_work: arXiv:2511.21730 (procedural memory retrieval benchmark) combined with arXiv:2602.02751 (strategy auctions). The proposal concedes both, correctly. 2511.21730 already establishes the mediator the paper depends on — that embedding retrievers on procedural items behave as unordered bags of words and cannot separate functionally distinct procedures — and 2602.02751 already establishes that the only real transition is M=0 to M>0. Between them, a reader has the mechanism and the saturation; what remains for this proposal is the end-to-end swap and the quantitative mapping. That is a real gap (neither re-runs the agent with the retriever frozen, neither token-matches), but it is an ablation-shaped gap, not a new phenomenon. The second threat is the long-context-vs-RAG literature, which the proposal engages only in prose (Related Work §7): the claim that retrieval's value is regime-dependent along a query-differentiation axis is not new there, and the proposal runs no factual-RAG cell, so its own stated falsifier ('if procedural and factual-RAG cells did not sit at opposite ends of the overlap axis, the law would be falsified') is asserted and never tested.
strongest_objection: The central law is close to analytic at the end where it will be confirmed. O = mean pairwise Jaccard of top-k sets is, by construction, a measure of how much A_ret's per-instance injected content differs from any fixed k-item block; as O -> 1, A_ret and A_fix are literally the same prompt on most instances, so R_fix ~ 0 is guaranteed by the manipulation check rather than discovered. 'Overlap predicts the retrieval premium' then reduces to 'the size of the outcome difference tracks the size of the treatment difference.' The non-trivial half of the law is the O < 0.25 end (Prediction 2: 'every cell with O < 0.25 has R_fix >= 8'), and there the design is anchored almost entirely on manufactured cells: B-dup is paraphrase near-duplicates seeded against specific test instances, and E-mix is a two-environment splice. After excluding B-dup as the proposal itself requires, the low-overlap end of a ~20-point regression rests on essentially E-mix (tested twice) — so the Spearman rho <= -0.6 requirement on non-synthetic cells is decided by one or two points. Compounding this, O is not independent of the knobs used to move it: mean pairwise Jaccard is mechanically a function of k and N, and k and N are two of the four 'independent' knobs, which also confounds Prediction 6 (V is compared across k=1 and k=7 cells whose O values differ partly because k differs). Second, load-bearing predictions are stated at thresholds their own MDEs cannot resolve. Prediction 4 — which the proposal itself calls 'the prediction that decides whether our claim is about procedural memory or only about template-repeating benchmarks' — is a difference-in-differences between E2-narrow (n=100, stated MDE ~9) and E2-broad (n=140, stated MDE ~8), so the SE on that >=3-point contrast is roughly 6 points; it is powered at a small fraction of what it claims, and 'R_fix < 2' cannot be established by TOST at margin 4 at n=100 by the proposal's own arithmetic (equivalence needs an observed gap <= 1.4 at n=600). Third, the cell accounting does not reconstruct: Prediction 1 asserts TOST passing in '>=8 of the ~11' O>0.5 cells, but the E1 table runs A_fix in only about six cells (B_expel N=500 and N=1000, the k=7 volume cell, B_rbank, E-mix-on-E1, B-dup) plus three on E2 and four cross-model — and the proposal states it will 'report per model and never pool,' which strands the cross-model cells. Fourth, gate G1 (every bank must beat A0 by >=8 points) is a precondition the memory literature and this track's own prior results suggest frequently fails; if it fails broadly, most cells become 'memory inert here' and the regression has no cells left, which is a plausible modal outcome rather than a tail risk. Finally, the headline that the diagnostic is 'computable in seconds, zero agent rollouts' is inconsistent with the fitted model, which conditions on acc(A_ret) - acc(A0) as a covariate and gates cells on G1 — both of which require rollouts. The LOO test uses O alone while the reported fit is covariate-adjusted; these are different models and the paper should not be allowed to advertise one and estimate the other.
what_would_fix_it: The cheapest and most decisive fix costs zero extra episodes: report R_fix restricted to the subset of instances on which the retrieved set actually differs from the frozen set. If per-instance conditioning is worthless even on the instances where it changes the prompt, the claim is empirical rather than definitional, and the paper survives the tautology objection that will otherwise sink it. Report that conditional R_fix alongside the marginal one in every high-overlap cell, and regress on it. Second, add a retrieval ceiling: an oracle or LLM-reranker read path (2511.21730's own finding is that LLM-generated abstractions transfer where embeddings do not), so a null can be attributed to query-conditioning rather than to weak dense/BM25/MMR retrievers. Third, re-power the E2 narrow-vs-broad contrast — it is the only within-environment, non-manufactured diversity manipulation in the design and is currently the weakest cell in the study; take episodes from the B_expel N in {250} bank sweep and the A_rand draws to bring both E2 cells toward n=400+, or demote Prediction 4 to descriptive and stop calling it decisive. Fourth, add at least one non-synthetic low-overlap cell that is not an environment splice (e.g., a genuinely heterogeneous single-environment suite, or WebArena/tool-agent tasks with distinct sub-goals) so the fitted crossing threshold is not carried by B-dup and E-mix. Fifth, decouple O from k: either report O at a fixed k for all cells, or fit R_fix on O with k and N as explicit covariates, so the law is not partly recovering an arithmetic identity. Sixth, either run one factual-RAG cell to test the low-overlap-limit claim, or delete that falsification condition from the paper.
missing_baseline: A retrieval upper bound. There is no oracle-retrieval or LLM-reranker arm establishing that per-instance conditioning has any headroom in this setup, so R_fix ~ 0 is ambiguous between 'the read path is decorative' and 'dense/BM25/MMR retrievers over strategy-level items are bag-of-words weak' — and 2511.21730, which the proposal cites approvingly, already reported the latter. Without a ceiling, the paper's title claim is unearned and a reviewer will demand the cell. Secondary omissions: (a) a best-fixed-subset arm chosen on dev to maximize accuracy rather than retrieval frequency — A_fix as specified (highest dev retrieval frequency) is not the strongest static competitor, which makes A_fix an odd primary arm to hang an equivalence claim on; and (b) a raw whole-bank-in-context arm at N=100, the direct long-context control the RAG parallel in Related Work §7 invites and that A_comp (frontier-compiled) does not substitute for.
preprint_collision: Among the more serious collision checks I have seen: it quotes specific text, names 2511.21730 as a real partial collision and concedes it, concedes outright that 2602.02751 scoops the bank-size saturation claim and demotes that claim accordingly, and explicitly withdraws five arXiv IDs relied on in a prior draft. That is the right behavior and I credit it. Three reservations keep it from being a clean pass. (1) The check itself discloses that an earlier draft of this same line of work cited arXiv IDs the author could not find in search results; that history should discount, not increase, a reviewer's confidence in the quoted passages here, several of which (2602.02751, 2605.20616, 2606.23127, 2606.29824, 2607.01480) I cannot verify and which are dated within the last several months. The proposal's own rule — nothing enters the novelty argument unless it appears in a quotable search result — is the right rule, but it does not make the quotes checkable by me. (2) No OpenReview or venue-submission sweep, which the proposal admits; a 'freeze the retrieved subset' ablation in the appendix of a combined-system submission is exactly the kind of thing that sweep would find, and it would remove the paper's primary arm. (3) The RAG-vs-long-context literature is engaged only in prose with no paper named, despite the proposal staking an explicit falsification condition on where factual-RAG cells sit on its overlap axis. Net: no preprint I can name already makes the full claim, but the check's own concessions leave the residual novelty thin — the direction is conceded as converging across 2511.21730, 2602.02751 and 2606.23127, so the paper stands or falls on the predictive law, which is the part most vulnerable to the tautology objection above.
